diagnosis: A PROD-01 worker closed NO_ALLOCATION before any authority attempt because the single allowed compact frontier read was truncated by the runtime. EFF023 existed but its 64 KB target and minified in-memory check did not bound the actual published transport tightly enough. The hot path therefore still allowed a connector-scale payload to defeat deterministic pool sharding.
intervention: Integrated and ratcheted the concurrent claim-frontier transport repair: the compiler now strips presentation-only preclaim metadata, preserves exact claim payload/source data, enforces a hard 24 KB serialized budget that may reduce candidate count before overflow, and publishes minified JSON. Updated EFF023 to the 24 KB transport contract with the observed PROD-01 failure as evidence, then corrected the ratchet checker to accept the implemented inclusive <=24 KB boundary.

checks: no published candidate missing claim_path or claim_payload_shape
ready, role_ready and recovery lanes all remain represented

remaining_boundary: The mechanism and its static guard are verified and a real published frontier is under the 24 KB cap. A fresh independent worker still needs to traverse the new frontier without ALLOCATOR_READ_TRUNCATED_BY_RUNTIME before EFF023 should be promoted from STATIC_GUARDED_PENDING_RUNTIME to runtime-observed/ratcheted.
